{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-sd-x","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"3bbd2bda161dfb7ee9a9bbfda78f664aa2aafd6104fe838def3c6091f39724ca","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-sd-class-std:lineage:64","source_registry_sha256":"a4e51960bfe4da242ea11046073ac8d3d0353ce120a5409a11c1f9ab4c4da57a","source_liveness_sha256":"1aea607665fc1312b9a6988c94545b32e414886d6d428b2b6d66e4261f9397f1"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Space management and communication","heading":"C2 — Knowledge continuation and confusables: Space management and communication","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Knowledge continuation and confusables: Space management and communication

FACT_ID: sec15-R01 | anchor: A55
High beams improve distant night visibility when there is no oncoming vehicle; the handbook describes the visible distance as twice that of low beams. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec15-R02 | anchor: A55
Dim high beams within 500 feet of an approaching vehicle. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec15-R03 | anchor: A55
Use low beams when following another vehicle at less than 500 feet or driving in heavy traffic. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec15-R04 | anchor: A55
Use low beams in fog, snow or heavy rain because reflected high-beam light causes glare; use fitted fog lamps in those conditions too. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec15-R05 | anchor: A55
Never drive with only the parking lamps illuminated. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec15-R06 | anchor: A55
If an oncoming driver does not dim, briefly flash the high beams; if glare continues, look toward the right road edge until that vehicle passes. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec15-R07 | anchor: A55
Daytime running lamps improve daytime visibility but do not replace headlights at night or in fog, rain or snow. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec15-R08 | anchor: A55
Without daytime running lamps, manually using headlights provides similar daytime visibility, but remember to turn them off after shutting down the engine. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec15-R09 | anchor: A55
Use the horn to communicate a crash risk, with a light tap when no immediate danger exists. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec15-R10 | anchor: A55
A light horn tap can warn a pedestrian or cyclist moving toward the lane, but at an intersection crossing yield instead of sounding the horn at them. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec15-R11 | anchor: A55
A light tap may warn a passed driver turning toward your lane or a driver who is inattentive or cannot see you. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec15-R12 | anchor: A55
A light horn warning may be useful where a steep hill, sharp curve or narrow alley exit blocks the view ahead. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec15-R13 | anchor: A55
Use a sharp horn blast when another vehicle may hit you or when your own uncontrolled vehicle is moving toward someone. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec15-R14 | anchor: A55
Do not use the horn to hurry a driver, criticize an error or greet a friend. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec15-R15 | anchor: A55
Do not sound the horn around blind pedestrians, animal-drawn vehicles or animals being herded on the road. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec15-R16 | anchor: A55
If a vehicle breaks down, warn others with flares or triangles behind it and contact authorities by phone if one is available. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec15-R17 | anchor: A55
For vehicle trouble, move off the road and away from traffic when possible and activate the 4-way emergency flashers. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec15-R18 | anchor: A55
If the disabled vehicle cannot get fully off the road, stop where it is visible rather than just past a hill or around a curve. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec15-R19 | anchor: A55
Stand safely away from the roadway and use available warning devices; never change a tire from within a traffic lane. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec15-R20 | anchor: A55
A raised hood or white cloth tied to the antenna, side mirror or door handle can signal a vehicle emergency. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec15-R21 | anchor: A56
Avoid another vehicle’s side-and-rear blind area by moving ahead or dropping back, and pass through that blind area promptly. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec15-R22 | anchor: A56
Do not remain directly beside or immediately behind a large truck or bus. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec15-R23 | anchor: A56
The handbook’s truck No Zone includes blind areas up to 20 feet in front of the cab, beside it and up to 200 feet behind. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec15-R24 | anchor: A56
As a rule of thumb, if the truck or bus driver is not visible in the side mirror, assume your vehicle is not visible to that driver. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec15-R25 | anchor: A56
Warn other drivers before changing direction or slowing so they have time to react. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec15-R26 | anchor: A56
Signal before lane changes, turns, merging, parking and both the start and finish of a pass, even when nobody else is apparent. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec15-R27 | anchor: A56
The handbook gives a turn-signal distance of 100 feet but warns against signaling before an intervening street, driveway or entrance where another driver could misunderstand. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec15-R28 | anchor: A56
If another vehicle may enter between you and the intended turn, pass that vehicle’s entry point before signaling the turn. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec15-R29 | anchor: A56
After a turn or lane change, confirm that the turn signal has stopped. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec15-R30 | anchor: A56
Slow as early as safely possible and tap the brake pedal 3 or 4 times before an unexpected slowdown or stop to warn following traffic. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec15-R31 | anchor: A56
Give advance slowdown warning for a turn without a separate turn lane, parking or turning just before an intersection, or a hidden road obstruction or traffic queue. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec15-R32 | anchor: A56
Hand signals can supplement turn lamps in bright sun or serve an antique vehicle built before July 1, 1958 that may lack those lamps. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec15-R33 | anchor: A56
For a left hand-and-arm turn signal, extend the hand straight outward. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec15-R34 | anchor: A56
For a right hand-and-arm turn signal, point the hand upward. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec15-R35 | anchor: A56
For a stop or slowdown hand signal, point the hand downward. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0056]
